name: Hiram (King of Tyre)
title: Solomon's Phoenician Allies
summary: Hiram was king of the Phoenician city of Tyre and a close ally of both King David and King Solomon. He provided materials and craftsmen for the construction of Solomon's temple in Jerusalem, and the two kings entered into extensive trade agreements that brought great wealth to both kingdoms.

keyEvents.title: Sent Materials to David's Palace
keyEvents.description: Hiram sent cedar trees, carpenters, and stonecutters to David to build his palace in Jerusalem as a sign of friendship between the two kings.

keyEvents.title: Agreement with Solomon on the Temple
keyEvents.description: When Solomon was building the temple, he made an agreement with Hiram for the delivery of cedar and cypress from Lebanon in exchange for wheat and oil.

keyEvents.title: Supplied Skilled Craftsmen
keyEvents.description: Hiram sent his best craftsmen, including a master bronze worker also named Hiram, to help with the construction and decoration of the temple.

keyEvents.title: Joint Trading Expeditions
keyEvents.description: Hiram and Solomon cooperated in sending fleets of ships to Ophir to bring back gold, silver, ivory, and other valuable goods.

keyEvents.title: Received twenty cities in Galilee
keyEvents.description: After the temple and the royal palace were completed, Solomon gave twenty cities in the region of Galilee to Hiram as payment, but Hiram was not satisfied with them.
